column1: # The cities with a prayer-times page on taqwa.world. One city per line, tab-separated:
# id         the city's GeoNames id in the app's shared/src/commonMain/composeResources/files/cities.csv;
#            the country, coordinates and time zone always come from there, never from here.
# languages  the page languages, space-separated; English is always one of them.
# featured   the languages whose home page lists the city.
# names      lang=Name pairs separated by ';', only where the app's own name is wrong or reads
#            badly as a page title. Every one here is a finding to fix in the app's city files.
# Nothing about the calculation is set here. A page shows exactly what the app shows a user in
# that city who has changed no setting: the country's method from CalculationMethodDefaults, the
# Standard Asr (the app has no country default for the Asr school yet), the automatic
# So a country is live only where that agrees, within about two minutes, with the timetable its
# mosques actually follow (the national authority's, or the dominant one where there is none).
# Everywhere else the rows are kept below, commented out, with what disagrees; each comes back by
# deleting its "# " once the app has the method. The checks were made on 25 September 2026
# against the official tables for September and October 2026 (sources in docs/BUILD-LOG.md).
# tools/timetables validates every row on every build: an unknown id, a duplicate slug, a page
# language with no name, or a featured language without a page fails the build.
# Saudi Arabia: Umm al-Qura, within a minute of second-hand copies of the official calendar.
# Before Ramadan (from 8 February 2027) the app needs Umm al-Qura's 120-minute Ramadan Isha; until
# it has it the generator refuses a Ramadan month here rather than show Isha half an hour early.

column1: # UAE: the Dubai method, within 2 minutes of the published Dubai table.
# Kuwait: the Kuwait method, within a minute of the ministry's calendar.
# held: Qatar. Calendar House puts Maghrib at sunset + 3 and Isha at Maghrib + 90; the app is 3 minutes early at both.
# held: Bahrain. The Supreme Council's calendar has Isha 4 minutes later than the app.
# held: Oman. The Ministry of Endowments' Dhuhr to Isha are 5 to 6 minutes later than the app's.
# held: Jordan. The Ministry of Awqaf's Maghrib is 7 and Isha 5 minutes later than the app's.
# held: Palestine. Gaza Awqaf (about 19.5°/17.5°, Maghrib + 3): the app's Fajr is 7 minutes late, Maghrib and Isha 3 early; no West Bank table was found.
# held: Lebanon. Dar al-Fatwa's Fajr is 9 minutes earlier and Maghrib 6 later than the app's; Shia calendars differ further.
# held: Syria. The Awqaf table (MWL plus a 2-minute margin) has Maghrib 2 minutes after the app's, and nothing newer than February 2026 to check.
# held: Iraq. The Sunni Endowment's Dhuhr is 4 minutes later than the app's; the Shia Endowment's Maghrib is about sunset + 15.
# held: Yemen. No published timetable could be found to check against.
# Egypt: the Egyptian method, within 2 minutes of the Survey Authority's table for all of September.
# held: Libya. The Awqaf and Dar al-Ifta table in use since 1994 (about 18.5° Fajr, 18.3° Isha, Dhuhr + 3, Maghrib + 3) has Isha 6 to 7 and Maghrib 3 to 4 minutes later than the app's MWL.
# held: Tunisia. The National Institute of Meteorology's Dhuhr is 6 to 7 and Isha 5 to 6 minutes later than the app's.
# held: Algeria. The ministry's calendar has Maghrib 3 to 4 minutes after the app's.

# held: Morocco. The Ministry of Habous (about 19°/17°, Dhuhr + 5, Maghrib + 4 to 5) differs from the app by 4 to 6 minutes, and the country left UTC+1 for UTC+0 on 20 September 2026 (tzdata 2026c), which the JDK does not have yet.
# held: Mauritania. The ministry's Fajr (19.5°) is 5 to 6 minutes earlier than the app's.
# held: Sudan. The Fiqh Academy's Fajr (19.5°) is about 6 minutes earlier than the app's.
# Türkiye: Diyanet, within 2 minutes of Diyanet's own tables for eight cities across October.
# held: Uzbekistan. The Muslim Board uses 15.5° for Fajr and Isha and the Hanafi Asr: Fajr is 13 minutes, Isha 12 and Asr about 49 away from the app's defaults.

# held: Pakistan and India. The Karachi seminaries' timetable matches the app's Karachi method within a minute, but with the Hanafi Asr, which mosques here follow; the app's default Asr is Standard, about 50 minutes earlier. Back when the app defaults to Hanafi here.
# held: Bangladesh. Hanafi Asr as above, and the Islamic Foundation adds 3 minutes to Fajr, Dhuhr and Maghrib.
# Singapore: the Singapore method, within a minute of MUIS for all of 2026.
# held: Indonesia. Kemenag adds about 2 minutes to its 20°/18° times; all five prayers are 2 to 3 minutes later than the app's.
# held: Malaysia. JAKIM moved Fajr to 18° in 2019; the app's Fajr is 8 to 12 minutes earlier.
# South Africa, Cape Town: the Muslim Judicial Council's times match the app's MWL exactly.
# held: Johannesburg, Pretoria and Durban. The Jamiatul Ulama tables use the Hanafi Asr (57 minutes later) with Dhuhr + 5 and Maghrib + 3.
# held: the rest of Africa. No national timetable was found to check (Nigeria, Senegal, Somalia), or the country was not checked yet.
# held: United Kingdom. Most large mosques use the London Unified Prayer Timetable, whose seasonal Fajr and Isha are 13 to 18 minutes later and 15 to 24 minutes earlier than the app's.
# held: France. No shared timetable: most Île-de-France mosques use about 12 to 13° for Fajr, the Grande Mosquée its own; the app's 18° Fajr is up to 34 minutes earlier.
# held: Belgium. The Executive of Muslims of Belgium's Isha is 6 to 7 minutes later than the app's.
# held: the Netherlands. No authority; three different timetables are in use, none within 7 minutes of the app.
# held: Germany. Most mosques follow DITIB and Diyanet, up to 9 minutes from the app.
# held: Bosnia, Kosovo and Albania. Their national calendars differ from the app by 7 to 11 minutes.
# held: Russia. The Spiritual Administration uses 18°/15°; the app's Fajr is 18 minutes later.
# held: the rest of Europe. Not checked yet.
# United States and Canada: no national authority. The app's ISNA method is what most ISNA
# mosques publish (within 3 minutes in New York and Toronto); the page says which method it is.
# held: Australia and New Zealand. No dominant body; Sydney's Lakemba Mosque is up to 17 minutes from the app, and New Zealand was not checked.
